svg.aria-label: Lending rAAPL. You lend 1,000 of rAAPL into the short market, nUSDC | rAAPL, and still follow Apple's price. A Leverage Short trader posts nUSDC as collateral, borrows the rAAPL and sells it, and pays interest that comes back to you. At 2 percent a year, 1,000 of rAAPL becomes 1,020 if the price is flat, 1,122 if it rises 10 percent, and 918 if it falls 10 percent, against 1,000, 1,100 and 900 from just holding. You can only recall what traders are not borrowing, and if a trader is liquidated for less than the debt, lenders can lose some rAAPL.
svg.title: Holders lend to the shorts
